title: Canonical-map identification for compact internal adjunction mates
statement: With the generic monoidal concrete etale coefficient hypotheses of compact internal adjunction [prop-asd-internal-adjunction], let (g-prime,f-prime,f,g) be a commuting square with compactifiable vertical maps, exceptional right adjoints and invertible compact projection maps. Let B:Rf-! ⋙ Lg-star → Lg-prime-star ⋙ Rf-prime-! be any invertible natural transformation and N∈D(X,A). Assume the compatibility of the projection squares for the pullback-composition square, the two pullback tensorators and inverse B. Then for every Q∈D(S,A), pullback of compact internal adjunction followed by internal-Hom pullback comparison and precomposition with inverse B at N equals ordinary base change [sbc-def-base-change-map], internal-Hom pullback comparison, the internal-Hom image of the exceptional mate of inverse B, and compact internal adjunction on the lower square. The statement is an explicit equality of the canonical maps, without a Cartesian or finiteness hypothesis beyond the stated compatibility.

source.place: Final paragraph: compatibility of compact projection, compact exchange, and the ordinary/exceptional adjunction pairings.

proof.text: Instantiate compactHomMonoidalCompatibility with TX = Lg-prime-star, TY = Lg-star, M = N, the pullback-composition square sigma, inverse compact exchange rho, and b = inverse of B at N. The assumed equality of projection squares is exactly its hypothesis.

Expand the canonical definitions: the mate of sigma is derivedBaseChangeMap, the tensorator mates are derivedHomUpperStarComparison, and the exceptional mate is mateEquiv of inverse B. The resulting equality is the displayed canonical compact-adjunction exchange square.
